## 1. Mandate

Pillar 3's thirteenth decision-record scenario. The scoping pass selected
the exported disk-interoperability pair `ms_import()` / `ms_export()`
(`R/io-catalog.R` -- the format enum with its deferred-WTSI clause, the file
gate, the header-anchor law, the channel-label three-way, the cell law, the
whole-number law, and the downstream signature validator) -- the face every
real COSMIC/SigProfiler round-trip rides on, adjudicated as a decision
record for the first time. The format enum carries a documented deferral:
`wtsi` is a KNOWN format whose long layout is deferred pending an upstream
specimen (the [V] discipline), so it aborts with the enum clause naming
exactly the verified pair `cosmic, sigprofiler` -- committed verbatim,
both bullet legs and the received-rendering. Everything here is closed-form
by construction: the plants are hand-written TSV bytes over scalar rationals,
the executed path touches no RNG (measured at both ends), no network, no
data objects, and there is no seed to pin. The R-bound benchmark runner, the
FFI shim and the declined calibration estimators are DECLINED scope and are
never invoked here.

## 2. The plant and the arms

The plant is hand-written TSV files and in-memory S7 objects fed to the
EXPORTED pair alone (the internal resolver table and the file-hash helper
are never reached directly; the dual-kernel hash check calls the shipped
canonical deriver exactly as the face itself does) -- D3 law: synthetic
plants only, zero COSMIC numeric matrices, zero real-data bytes; "COSMIC"
and "sigprofiler" appear solely as FORMAT NAMES. The 36-arm frozen law
roster splits by observed class exactly as measured: 4
`msuiter_error_option` (the format enum and its case/unknown variants),
24 `msuiter_error_input` (the file gate, the header anchor, the
channel-label three-way, the cell law and the whole-number law), 5
`msuiter_error_signature` (the validator's nonnegativity, NA/finite and
all-NA arms downstream of a syntactically clean import), and 3 base
`simpleError` arms whose messages are locale-variable (the `kind`
match.arg rejects, the empty file, the directory-as-file) -- committed
CLASS-ONLY so the law never freezes a translator's wording. Two witness
arms ride the stable3 mode (every frozen bullet must be found inside the
live message, in any locale, without verbatim equality). The 13-arm spec
witness covers the accepted round-trips end to end; a 3-arm precedence
witness and a 4-token fidelity drill commit the discriminators below.

## 3. The measured laws this scenario commits

- **The reader-coercion law split.** `read.delim` type-converts before any
  validator sees a cell: the literals `NaN`, `NA`, `""` and `Inf` are
  COERCED into numeric NAs and die on the whole-number law, while only the
  non-coercible `'abc'` reaches the cell law -- the two laws never trade an
  arm, and the split is committed per arm from the observed class and
  clause.
- **The locked provenance pair.** An imported object's
  `build` is `"imported:sha256=<64 hex>"`, its `n_samples` is the integer
  `0L` and its `exposures` matrix is the `k x 0` companion -- committed as
  one locked trio, plus the channel-hash chain: the 64-hex
  `channel_hash`, the recomputed `msuiter_hash_labels` byte, the
  `hashes-agree` bit and the `build-carries-filehash` bit.
- **The dual-kernel SHA-256 agreement.** The canonical pure-R deriver
  (`.ms_fit_sha256`, the very helper the face itself uses) and the
  `digest` accelerator agree on the plant bytes -- both hex strings and the
  agreement bit committed; the plant text is the frozen echo table itself,
  so the checksum rides over committed bytes, never a float rendering.
- **The 17-significant-digit round-trip drill.** Four planted rationals
  render through the sanctioned R printer to four 17-significant-digit
  tokens committed as a SEALING-PLATFORM CENSUS RECORD (the windows
  fan-out leg later witnessed that these renderings drift by an ULP across
  platforms and are not round-trip secure even within one process -- see
  item (v); they are therefore never live byte-equality targets). The
  live-side law compares STRUCTURE (each token is a 22-character glyph)
  and NUMERIC identity (`all.equal` at the base's natural tolerance)
  against the freshly exported bytes; the reader-faithfulness bit -- the
  96-row column is the four as-read token doubles recycled identically 24
  times -- rides `identical()` over same-parser bytes. The `%.20g`
  renderings and the drift bits beyond the 17th digit are committed as
  payload CENSUS only (finite, in-domain), never as equality targets: the
  D11 posture -- full-precision float equality seals platform DETs, not
  laws.
- **The precedence discriminators.** Where two laws could speak, the
  committed winner is named: the file gate outranks the format enum when
  both are violated; the header-anchor law outranks the label three-way
  when the plant breaks both; coercibility decides cell-vs-whole-number
  (above). Each discriminator carries its anti-arm so the ordering can
  never silently swap.
- **Instrument failures caught fail-closed, again threefold.** (i) The
  harness/standalone split: the 31 full-mode message arms reddened inside
  `test_file` while the identical bytes were green standalone -- the
  LocationReporter census spoke zero diff blocks (a silent census), so the
  adjudication was re-armed through the SummaryReporter, which named the
  survivor: a bullet riding the live message. (ii) The bullet bytes were
  then measured at both ends -- the harness renders `"i "` (`69 20`), the
  standalone Rscript renders `"ℹ "` (`e2 84 b9 20`) -- and the strip's
  ASCII leg was found dead: on this base `sub(fixed = TRUE)` is a LITERAL
  SUBSTRING op, so the anchored pattern `"^i "` can never match, silently;
  the careteless glyph leg had masked it outside the harness. The strip now
  tests explicit prefixes (`startsWith` + `substring`). (iii) The fidelity
  unit's `all.equal(...)$equal` aborted `"$ operator is invalid for atomic
  vectors"` -- on this base `all.equal()` returns an ATOMIC verdict -- and
  the law was repaired to `isTRUE(all.equal(x, y))`. Earlier in the same
  chain: empty witness cells read back as `NA` under `na.strings = ""`,
  so absent renderings ride the explicit `"(none)"` sentinel behind the
  finiteness census. (iv) The installed-context split: the full local
  `devtools::check` gate reddened 18 while every pkgload-mode census was
  green -- under check the seven checkout-reading units met an
  unlocatable root and FAILED instead of skipping. They now open with the
  sanctioned `is.na(.ms_root)` skip idiom (the CS-12/gallery pattern);
  both worlds verified -- repo-mode census unchanged at 253/0/0/0,
  NA-root simulation skips the seven with zero failures. (v) The ubuntu
  AND windows fan-out legs each reddened three arms (same root causes on
  both sides), and the forensics found TWO real
  defects on our side of the D11 line: (va) the plant files were written
  through the TEXT channel, so platform EOL bytes leaked into the file
  SHA-256 provenance (darwin-sealed `5350e3..` vs windows-minted
  `84cfbd..`) --
  repaired by a binary-channel writer (`open = "wb"` around `writeLines`)
  at all four plant sites, pinning EOL so the hash is platform-invariant;
  (vb) the fidelity law byte-compared LIVE 17-digit printer renderings --
  itself a D11 violation, witnessed when windows rendered `..68` where
  darwin committed `..69` (and `..00` vs `..02` on a second token). The
  reformation makes the token column a committed-vs-committed census
  record and moves every live comparison to structure (`nchar == 22`) plus
  `all.equal`; the re-export identity bit that repair had briefly added
  then failed even on darwin -- a probe witnessed the `..69` glyph
  re-exporting as `..68` in the SAME process (the 17-digit rendering of
  a halfway double is not round-trip secure on this base) -- so it was
  deleted as structurally unsound rather than platform-specific. Net law:
  no live float-byte equality anywhere in the drill; final census
  254/0/0/0, runner `OVERALL PASS (159)` with the five witnesses
  double-minted `DET` 5/5. All are
  OBSERVATION-instrument failures caught by the
  project's own laws before any verdict was committed, never verdict
  failures.

## 4. Hard rails and postures

The hard rails: the ten banned-token greps in the law file (no
`msuiter:::` namespace reach, no internal resolver table, no
`.ms_io_file_sha256`, no validator-by-name, no `expect_` in the runner, no
declined-calibration trio, no benchmark driver, no `set.seed`/`sample(`,
no `download.file`/`http`); the hard shape gates (13/36/3/4/9 rows over
the five witnesses); the RNG-purity rail measured at both ends of the
runner's own process via `.Random.seed` presence (the `sample.kind`
accessor does not exist on this base); the plant-checksum dual-kernel
identity; and the pre-write witness-finiteness census (no cell empty,
NA-bearing, delimiter-carrying or quote-opening). Postures: DECISION RECORD
only -- the face's contract behavior on planted truth, no extraction claim,
no benchmark claim, no format-conformance claim about the deferred WTSI
layout; the D11 float posture honored by construction (byte-freezes are
integer, label, class and clause bytes only; the 17-digit token column is a
committed sealing-platform census record, never a live equality target);
the pillar-2 namespace-reach
idiom is banned in the law file and grepped away, as are the
declined-family names and the FFI shim.
